Subject: Usage spike and renewal ahead — quick sync?

Kim —

Quick note from our side: over the last 10 days we saw a ~3.8x spike in generation traffic vs. our July baseline. The spike seems concentrated on a new feature we rolled (interactive summarization) and we're burning through daily tokens faster than expected. Renewal is 2027-09-30 and we need to understand options so we don't run into throttles or massive overages.

High level:
- Avg tokens/day (Jul): ~8.2M
- Peak tokens/day (Aug week 3): ~31M
- Current committed monthly tokens: 240M (12-month term)

A few asks: can we get a quick runbook on short-term burst protection, a proposal for a commit uplift, and a quick ROI sketch showing cost per 1k tokens vs. expected reduction if we enable batching/caching suggestions? We have Alice (engineering) copied — she'd join a call if helpful.

Thanks,
Ben

HelixAI

- Temporary burst credits (1–2 weeks) to avoid throttling while we finalize a new commit,
- Short-term routing to a higher-capacity pool for the most latency-sensitive endpoints,
- Quick batching prefix for the summarization endpoint (low lift on our side, medium ROI).

I can send a short post-call recap and a preliminary ROI table (tokens -> $) that maps three commitment tiers. Are you available tomorrow 10:30–11:00 PT?

From: kimberly_park@redwood.com

Date: 2027-08-29 15:20:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: HelixAI capacity pulse — summary & proposed action

Thanks for the quick call earlier — summary + next steps below. Rachel (CS) and Grace (Solutions) are looped for operational and technical validation.

What we observed
- Confirmed: recent feature roll increased calls with longer completion lengths (median completion tokens up ~2.6x).
- Token mix: ~65% generation, 25% embeddings, 10% reranking/others (from inspected traces).
- Spike drivers: parallelization on the client side + minimal batching at request-time.

Short-term mitigations (immediate, low-friction)
- 2 weeks of burst credits: +120M tokens (applied immediately) — prevents throttles while we finalize a commit.
- Route the summarization endpoint to our higher-throughput pool during peak hours (we can set a 9–18 PT window).
- Enable server-side batching for the summarization model (Grace to confirm infra changes).

Proposed term amendment (recommended)
- Current commit: 240M/month (12mo) at $0.0026 / 1k tokens (example).
- Proposal A (conservative): raise to 360M/month (12mo); incremental price: $0.0024 / 1k; includes 2 weeks burst credit now + 10% off overage for first quarter post-renewal.
- Proposal B (growth): raise to 480M/month (12mo); incremental price: $0.0022 / 1k; includes burst credit, priority routing, and a one-time $30k implementation credit for batching work.

Preliminary ROI sketch (monthly view)
- If HelixAI elects Proposal A and enables batching/caching improvements, our estimate: ~18–24% effective token reduction in high-volume windows -> estimated ~$6–10k/mo savings vs. unmanaged overage.

Immediate asks / owners
- Ben / Alice: confirm whether you want the burst credits applied immediately (we can turn on today).
- Rachel: confirm any contractual constraints for a 12mo amendment and whether legal needs redlines.
- Grace: validate feasibility and estimate for server-side batching (ETA: 3–5 business days).

Attachments included: helix_monthly_usage_jul-aug-2027.csv, latency_report_aug-2027.pdf
Links: HubSpot deal HD-9876 (https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/1234567/deal/HD-9876)

I'll draft the amendment once we have Ben's preference on Proposal A vs B and internal signoff.

Thanks —Kim

--

From: grace_oconnor@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Post-call: HelixAI capacity pulse — summary & proposed action

Quick technical notes from the solutions team — copying the call notes into this thread.

- Server-side batching: feasible with minimal code changes on our side. We batch by prompt template and sequence length buckets; expected rollout time 3 business days after a short validation window. Estimated engineering effort (Redwood): ~2 dev-days + 1 QA day.
- Caching: prefix caching can reduce redundant token generation for common system prompts; applies immediately if HelixAI standardizes prompt prefixes.
- Expected token reduction: conservative 10% steady-state; 18–24% during peak windows where parallel requests collapse into fewer batched RPCs.

Attachments: batching_reco.md (contains example curl snippets, migration checklist, and quick perf expectations).

Operational note: we can enable burst credits today; to do so we need Ben's explicit OK and a billing trigger to record the temporary credit period.

—Grace
Grace O'Connor
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
